title: A history of secrets
intro: Follow two thousand years of secret writing, from a general's shifted letters to the keys that protect your phone today.
outro: You broke a Roman shift, a Renaissance keyword, a wartime Enigma and a modern public key. Each fell to the same idea: find the weakness in how the key is used.
h1.story: Rome: a message shifted by a few letters. Try every shift.
h2.story: Another Roman dispatch. Letter counts give the shift away.
h3.story: A longer Roman order: confirm your shift on the whole text.
h4.story: The Renaissance brings keywords. One shift is no longer enough.
h5.story: Find the length of the keyword before you try to guess it.
h6.story: A longer secret, protected by a longer keyword.
h7.story: Wartime: the Enigma machine scrambles every letter differently.
h8.story: The same machine, a different starting position.
h9.story: Operators were careless. Use what you know about the message.
h10.story: Today: public keys. Anyone can lock, only the key owner can unlock.
h11.story: Small numbers are easy to factor. That is the weakness.
h12.story: Put it all together and read the final message.
